claims.claim: Measured absolute oral bioavailability in humans for structurally related amide/heteroaromatic drugs is predominantly above 20%: imidafenacin 57.8%, tolvaptan 56%, ACT-1004-1239 53%, lenvatinib in the order of 85%, and bromazepam 86%.
Venadaparib, which shares a benzamide/indazole-type core with the query, showed good oral bioavailability in patients and 70.63% oral bioavailability in mice.

New L2 data show that apatinib, a pyridine-containing oral amide, has human oral bioavailability of only 10–20% and low dog values, so the pyridine-amide analogy is not uniformly high-F; this weakens but does not overturn the overall supportive pattern.

L2 records for imidafenacin confirm the human absolute F of 57.8% and show lower F in rats (5.6%) and dogs (36.1%), indicating species dependence; the human value remains the most transferable reference.
